sources.quote: including land on the east bank of the Chao Phraya River, opposite his palace and enclosed by city walls, on which to settle their community.
Rama I had the Teochew resettle in the area of Sampheng, on the river's east bank southeast and downstream from the city centre.

facts.rationale: Resolved to contradicted/false (Wikipedia Chinatown, Bangkok): Teochew merchants were already settled on the east bank under King Taksin (1767-1782) and were relocated to Sampheng in 1782; they did not first come to the Bangkok area after 1782. Both quotes verified on the page.

sources.quote: Yaowarat is a road with a length of about 1.5 km (0.93 mi), 20 m (65 ft) wide and takes 8 years to build (1892–1900).

facts.rationale: Resolved to contradicted/numeric_off (Wikipedia Yaowarat Road): the road was built 1892-1900, so it cannot have been the commercial heart for 'over two centuries' (about 130 years). The same article's loose '200 years' refers to the Chinese trading community moving from its old site, not the road, and says 'some 200', not 'over'.

Resolved to unverifiable: gold shops and preserved food goods are on Wikipedia Yaowarat Road, but neon signage, apothecaries and a streetscape that 'retains much of its 19th- and early-20th-century character' were not found in any reliable source. trip_leak=false: a description of the district's character, not of visitor access or activities (consistent with F7c898538/Fe683dca7, which both labellers marked false).
